parts.text: In this experiment, you are to compare the combined resistance of lamps arranged in series and in parallel. Carry out the following instructions, referring to Fig. 3.1 and Fig. 3.2. The circuit shown in Fig. 3.1 has been set up for you. Fig. 3.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Switch on. Measure and record in Table 3.1 the current I in the circuit and the p.d. V across the two lamps. Switch off.

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Calculate the combined resistance R of the two lamps using the equation R = V I . Record this value of R in Table 3.1. Table 3.1 V / I / R / Fig. 3.1 Fig. 3.2 [4]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Complete the column headings in the table.

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Disconnect the lamps and the voltmeter. Set up the circuit shown in Fig. 3.2. Fig. 3.2

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) Switch on. Measure and record in Table 3.1 the current I in the circuit and the p.d. V across the two lamps. Switch off.

parts.label: f
parts.text: (f) Calculate the combined resistance R of the two lamps using the equation R = V I . Record this value of R in Table 3.1.

parts.label: g
parts.text: (g) Using the values of resistance obtained in (b) and (f) , calculate the ratio y of the resistances using the equation y = resistance of lamps in series resistance of lamps in parallel . y = ...................................................... [3]

parts.label: i
parts.text: (h) (i) Fig. 3.3 shows a circuit including two motors A and B . Fig. 3.3 Draw a diagram of the circuit using standard circuit symbols. The circuit symbol for a motor is: M An engineer wishes to measure the voltage across motor A .

parts.text: (ii) On Fig. 3.3 mark with the letters X and Y where the engineer should connect the voltmeter.
